analysis:
All units in this batch are documentation only. They cover CHANGELOG.md (the displayed head excerpts are old release history, lines 4531-5371, plus a v0.10.10 candidate section described in the patch excerpt), the removal of the changelog.d/feature-waitlists.md fragment, and docs/operations/provider-release.md (a version/date bump with a rewritten release description). No executable code, wire protocol, key handling, attestation, encryption or authorization logic changed in the supplied evidence, so no threat-model control (TB-002, TB-003, TB-007, TB-011, T-041, etc.) is weakened by these edits.

The removed fragment and the changelog patch describe a waitlist gate: darkbloom waitlist, and approval required for a new sandbox setup or new cluster pair. This is a client-side feature in code that is not in this batch. It touches TB-013 (sandbox installer, T-061) and TB-014 (GPU limit, T-062) only through a coordinator-side approval check. The changelog says that when the coordinator offers no waitlists, setup proceeds as before. That fail-open behavior is a product gating policy, not a security control, and the actual implementation is not visible here. Whether the CLI correctly treats waitlist approval as non-authorizing for sandbox installer or GPU-limit execution, and whether the waitlist call sends no Mac-identifying data as claimed, cannot be verified from these docs. Reviewers of the code PR should confirm that the waitlist check does not replace the existing owner confirmation and administrator prompt in TB-014, and that the waitlist HTTP call uses the existing authenticated, TLS-validated coordinator channel. The truncated provider-release.md excerpt contains no visible security-relevant claims that contradict the threat model. I identified no regression and have no basis for a finding. needs_deeper_review is set because the code implementing the waitlist behavior was not supplied.
